factual_claims.claim: Women are over-represented in administrative, clerical, and service jobs that are vulnerable to AI disruption.
Women are under-represented in STEM fields, limiting their access to high-paying AI-related jobs.
AI systems trained on biased datasets have been documented to discriminate in hiring, lending, and healthcare.
AI adoption could widen existing gender pay gaps.
Women perceive AI to be riskier than men.
factual_claims.claim_label: Gender Gap in AI Risk Perception

factual_claims.claim: Women exhibit higher levels of risk aversion than men.
AI systems improved from solving 4.4% of coding problems in 2023 to 71.7% in 2024.
Workplace adoption of AI among U.S. workers reached 46% in mid-2025.
Women are approximately 20% less likely than men to use generative AI tools.
Men's research productivity increased 6.4% more than women's following ChatGPT's release.
Workers without a university degree face higher levels of exposure to technological change than those with a degree.
Women are more exposed to AI across both high-complementarity and high-substitution roles than men.
